limits: One sequential ordered pair per engine; no randomized repeats or causal speed claim. Live Hub target counts differ (293/294) and may change.

Both modes have the same upload/CPU observers enabled and static matrices, shader warmup and texture-preparation options disabled. Chromium and Firefox preserve their different native DPR/buffer sizes; compare options within an engine, not raw FPS across engines.
Model/graphics jobs idle is a sampled interval, not exact completion or successful loading of every texture/entity. Eight original-image failures remain visible in each first-idle snapshot.
Initial-admission HTTP aggregates span the entire first admission until Leave, including later walking traffic; async request/phase duration sums are not elapsed wall time.

Upload buckets span both admissions, separated by phase. Dropped records and exhausted 1024-source identity capacity censor all four profiles; existing call durations include CPU/driver submission, not pure GPU time.
The one-shot census ran after initial walking/screenshot and before Leave; all four hit the 75ms CPU budget and are partial. Zero observed matching groups cannot establish full-scene absence.
Bitmap live bytes/leases are snapshots while models remain alive. These captures do not independently prove post-Leave resource closure; standalone ownership tests cover that separately.
No asset URLs, names, entity/participant identities, raw poses, credentials, account profiles, hardware/device identifiers or audio are published.
No public-world edits, microphone request or world interaction; thirty-minute endurance was cancelled. Firefox still fails all four fluid gates in both modes.
